description.value: Using psychophysiological interaction analyses of functional magnetic resonance imaging data, we examined changes in inter-regional connectivity between the amygdala and IFG with other brain regions during reappraisal of emotional responses and used emotion regulation success as an explicit regressor.

spans.text: Using psychophysiological interaction analyses of functional magnetic resonance imaging data, we examined changes in inter-regional connectivity between the amygdala and IFG with other brain regions during reappraisal of emotional responses and used emotion regulation success as an explicit regressor.

value: We hypothesized that the IFG is involved in linking the prefrontal control system to regions that are directly related to basal emotion processing (such as the amygdala) in order to orchestrate emotion regulatory processes.

we expected that (i) enhanced connectivity within the prefrontal network including lateral (VLPFC, DLPFC) and medial PFC regions (ventromedial and dorsomedial PFC; VMPFC and DMPFC) would correlate with reappraisal success, and (ii) enhanced coupling between the amygdala and PFC would predict reappraisal success.
